Thanks again for taking the time this morning — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so everyone has clear action items.

What we covered
- Goals: move critical inference workloads to Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency and better unit economics.
- Integration scope: SDK + tokenized auth, routing by model & priority, structured output/tool-calling for agent flows, embeddings for search & reranking.
- Capacity ask: you called out spikes and <150ms target at p95 for inference on short prompts.

Key technical notes (high level)
- SDK: our SDK supports streaming, tool-calling, and structured JSON output. We’ll provide a sample repo and quickstart.
- Auth: token-based with optional mTLS for Private deployments. For Dedicated we typically integrate via customer API key + IP allowlist.
- Routing: policy-based routing (latency-first for premium routes, cost-first for background jobs).
- Embeddings/reranker: we recommend computing embeddings offline and using a lightweight reranker in the Dedicated pool for low-latency re-ranks.

- Aditya: technical workshop to map request patterns to instance sizing (ETA: Tue 3/30).

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — autoscaling / throughput & queue sizing follow-up

Great call — adding some SE-level details so we can converge on sizing and integration work. Below are concrete items and assumptions that will affect autoscaling, queue sizing, and concurrency.

Assumptions we used for the attached sizing workbook
- Baseline payload: avg request -> 300 tokens generated (response), 80 tokens prompt.
- Model: family similar to 7B-quantized runtime (throughput numbers in workbook). If you plan to use a larger model, let us know — numbers change.
- Latency target: p95 < 150ms for the interactive route. Background/batch jobs can accept higher latency.

Autoscaling & throughput guidance
- Target concurrency per GPU: ~6-12 live requests for 7B-quantized depending on batching and KV cache hit rate.
- Queue sizing: configure a request queue with a short headroom buffer to absorb bursts; we typically start with max_queue_latency_ms=150 and max_queue_length = peak_qps * 10s to avoid rejecting sustained bursts.
- Scaling policy: scale up when average utilization > 70% for 60s; scale down after utilization < 40% for 5 minutes. Add cooldowns to prevent flapping.
- Warm pools: maintain a small warm pool (1-2 nodes) for predictable p95 on warm-started models.

Auth & SDK notes
- SDK: sample code for streaming + tool-calling attached in the quickstart repo (I'll paste link as soon as it's public). We support structured JSON outputs and schema enforcement at the SDK level to reduce parsing errors.
- Auth: for Dedicated we recommend API keys rotated via your KMS and IP allowlist. For Private, we can enable mTLS and CIP rules.

Routing & fallbacks
- Suggest two logical routes: interactive (low-latency, reserved concurrency) and batch (cost-optimized, preemptible).
- Fallbacks: a cheaper model family as automatic fallback when under heavy load to preserve availability.

Data points we need from Acme
- Peak QPS (15-min and 1-min), average QPS, average tokens per request, SLA target (p95).
- Percent of traffic that requires tool-calling / structured output vs plain generation (so we can reserve concurrency for the most latency-sensitive flows).

Attachment: dedicated-sizing-estimate.xlsx (updated with runtime assumptions).
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/123456789

Once you send the traffic profiles I’ll update the workbook and propose a concrete Dedicated capacity commit (nodes + warm pool + autoscaling policy) and an initial cost estimate.

- Aditya

Thanks for the traffic profile, Sarah — very helpful. Quick answers and next steps below.

Answers to your questions
1) Canary strategy: we recommend a staged rollout — (a) deploy to a 5% canary pool pinned to the new model/variant, (b) run synthetic heartbeats and smoke tests for 30-60 minutes, (c) gradually ramp to 25% then 100% with monitoring alerts on p95 and error rates. Use automatic rollback on >5% error increase or p95 degradations.
2) Billing: reserved nodes (committed Dedicated capacity) are billed as part of the commit. Warm pool nodes are charged at a reduced standby rate (we’ll surface both numbers in the SOW).

Proposed immediate next steps
- Aditya: update the sizing workbook with Acme numbers and propose a node & warm-pool config (ETA: Mon 3/29).
- Marissa: schedule a 90-min tech workshop (SE + Eng) to finalize integration touch points and run a quick smoke POC. I’ll propose times for week of 3/29.
- Acme: confirm preferred dates and any internal security reviewers we should loop in (SOC2 evidence will be requested later in the process).

Links & attachments
